This is a website for FIRE based content (Financially dependent retire early) and I want to start with single actual hourly wage calculator from the book Money or your life by Vicki Robin. Then I want to add new content based on this list Core calculators and “true cost” tools
    •    Actual Hourly Wage (front page): your v1, with saved presets (commute mode, work wardrobe, etc.).
    •    Job Profit/Loss Scorecard: converts a job into net weekly or monthly “life energy” after costs (money + time).
    •    Commute Cost Analyzer: true cost per commute (fuel + depreciation + parking + insurance delta + time + stress slider).
    •    Work Convenience Spending Tracker: “I bought lunch because I was tired” estimator; shows annualized impact.
    •    Subscription Burn Meter: total monthly subs → years-to-FI impact at your savings rate.
    •    Lifestyle Inflation Detector: compares spending over time; flags “quiet upgrades” (delivery, convenience, small recurring spends).
    •    Raise / Bonus Reality Check: shows after-tax gain, plus whether it meaningfully changes FI date (and how much).

FIRE planning that stays grounded
    •    FI Number Builder: target expenses × chosen multiple (25x, 30x, custom) with assumptions you can tweak.
    •    Savings ual “each 1% savings rate changes date by X”.
    •    “Cut $100” Impact Cards: choose a category cut (e.g., $100/mo) → see FI date shift and “life energy” regained.
    •    Expense Baseline Tool: guided flow to build “barebones / comfortable / deluxe” monthly budgets.
    •    LeanFIRE vs CoastFIRE vs BaristaFIRE Explorer: scenario toggles, side-by-side.
    •    One-Time Purchase Decision Tool: converts purchases to “hours of life energy” + opportunity cost at expected return.

Time, energy, and happiness accounting
    •    Time Budget Dashboard: where time goes weekly (work, commute, chores, sleep) → highlights reclaim opportunities.
    •    Chore ROI Calculator: “Should I outsource cleaning?” based on your actual hourly wage and happiness/time value.
    •    Stress Tax Slider: optional subjective cost for high-stress jobs that adjusts “true wage” (transparent and user-controlled).
    •    “Enough” Meter: a guided exercise to define “what’s enough” (spending and time) and track drift.

Casy Fund Planner: target months of expenses, but also “time-to-replace-income” risk rating.
    •    Burn Rate & Runway: for people transitioning to self-employment or semi-retirement.
    •    Big Expense Sinking Funds: car replacement, travel, home maintenance; keeps “annual surprises” honest.
    •    Insurance Coverage Checklist + Estimator: not quotes, just planning: what you have, what gaps mean financially.

Investing and withdrawal tools (careful, but useful)
    •    Simple Portfolio Tracker (manual input): balances by bucket (taxable, retirement, cash), no brokerage linking required.
    •    Withdrawal Strategy Sandbox: compare 4% rule vs variable spending vs guardrails (educational, not advice).
    •    Sequence-of-Returns “Bad Timing” Demo: interactive chart to show why buffers matter.
    •    Tax-Aware Drawdown Planner (later): rough brackets + withdrawal order scenarios, with clear disclaimers.

Habit and behavior features (what keeps people using the site)
    •    Weekly “1 Change” Challenge: pick one tweaed annual + FI-date impact.
    •    Goal System in “Life Energy” Units: goals expressed as hours/week reclaimed, not just money.
    •    Decision Journal: log big spending decisions and later reflect on whether they increased happiness.
    •    Milestone Badges: net worth milestones are common; yours could be “commute hours eliminated,” “subscriptions halved,” etc.

Content + tools that feel like a “workbench”
    •    Personal Playbooks: templates like “Reduce car dependence,” “Cut food spend without misery,” “Downsize plan.”
    •    Case Studies: anonymized “before/after” spending + true hourly wage transformations.
    •    Interactive Checklists: “prep for sabbatical,” “prep for quitting,” “first year of semi-retirement.”

Community features (optional, but sticky)
    •    Anonymous Benchmarks: compare spending categories by household type and location band (privacy-first).
    •    Scenario Sharing: share a FI plan link without revealing identity.
    •    Local Groups Directory: simple lisX touches that match the vibe
    •    All outputs in plain language: “This costs you 14 work-hours per month.”
    •    Annualized numbers everywhere: monthly → yearly → “years-to-FI” effect.
    •    Assumption transparency: every result shows what inputs drove it.
    •    Privacy-first mode: no account needed; export/import a local file. and 3. Just a react based, site with node based middleware running inside a vercel page.
